column3: The Hebrew has being called blessed in the passive and ends by addressing You in a plea not to surrender him; BSB keeps the LORD as acting subject throughout.
The Hebrew changes to You and says his whole bed was turned in sickness; BSB keeps a third-person subject and describes restoration from the bed.
The Hebrew explicitly names his soul; BSB says heal me.
The Hebrew says his name should perish; BSB says be forgotten.
The Hebrew makes his heart the subject of gathering wickedness; BSB describes the visitor gathering slander in his heart.
The Hebrew names something destructive without separately naming a disease; BSB explicitly says a vile disease.
The Hebrew calls him a man of his peace and describes making his heel great against him; BSB says close friend and lifted his heel.
The Hebrew names a triumphant shout; BSB says triumph.
